cards.front: In osteoporosis, what is wrong with the bone, and what do the serum calcium, phosphate, ALP and PTH show?
cards.back: Bone **mass is reduced**, but the matrix that remains is **normally mineralized**. Trabecular bone is lost first, so **vertebral compression**, hip and distal radius fractures are typical. Serum calcium, phosphate, ALP and PTH are all **normal**.
cards.back_pt: A **massa óssea está reduzida**, mas a matriz restante é **normalmente mineralizada**. O osso trabecular é perdido primeiro, por isso são típicas as fraturas por **compressão vertebral**, de quadril e de rádio distal. Cálcio, fósforo, fosfatase alcalina e PTH séricos são todos **normais**.

cards.front: What mutation causes achondroplasia, and which type of bone formation does it impair?
cards.back: A **gain-of-function FGFR3** mutation (autosomal dominant) inhibits chondrocyte proliferation in the growth plate. **Endochondral ossification** is impaired, so the **limbs are short**; membranous bone is spared, so the head looks relatively large. Most cases are **new mutations** linked to **advanced paternal age**.
cards.back_pt: Mutação de **ganho de função no FGFR3** (autossômica dominante) que inibe a proliferação dos condrócitos da placa de crescimento. A **ossificação endocondral** fica prejudicada: **membros curtos**; o osso membranoso é poupado e a cabeça parece relativamente grande. A maioria dos casos decorre de **mutações novas**, ligadas à **idade paterna avançada**.

cards.front: What is the defect in osteopetrosis, and what are its main consequences?
cards.back: **Osteoclasts cannot resorb bone**; one classic cause is **carbonic anhydrase II** deficiency (too little acid in the resorption pit). Bones become dense but **brittle**. Bone fills the marrow, causing **pancytopenia** and extramedullary hematopoiesis; narrow foramina cause **cranial nerve palsies**.
cards.back_pt: Os **osteoclastos não conseguem reabsorver osso**; uma causa clássica é a deficiência de **anidrase carbônica II** (pouco ácido na lacuna de reabsorção). Os ossos ficam densos, mas **frágeis**. O osso ocupa a medula, causando **pancitopenia** e hematopoese extramedular; forames estreitados causam **paralisias de nervos cranianos**.

cards.front: What lab pattern and complications are typical of Paget disease of bone?
cards.back: **Isolated high alkaline phosphatase**; calcium, phosphate and PTH are normal. Complications: bone pain, increasing **hat size**, **hearing loss**, **high-output heart failure** (vascular shunts in bone), fractures, and **osteosarcoma**.
cards.back_pt: **Fosfatase alcalina elevada isoladamente**; cálcio, fósforo e PTH normais. Complicações: dor óssea, **aumento do tamanho do chapéu**, **perda auditiva**, **insuficiência cardíaca de alto débito** (shunts vasculares no osso), fraturas e **osteossarcoma**.

cards.front: What causes McCune-Albright syndrome, and what are its three main features?
cards.back: A postzygotic (mosaic) **activating GNAS mutation**. Features: **polyostotic fibrous dysplasia** (bone replaced by fibrous tissue and irregular woven bone), **café-au-lait spots** with jagged *coast of Maine* borders, and endocrine overactivity, most often **precocious puberty**.
cards.back_pt: Uma **mutação ativadora do GNAS** pós-zigótica (mosaico). Achados: **displasia fibrosa poliostótica** (osso substituído por tecido fibroso e osso imaturo, não lamelar, irregular), **manchas café com leite** de bordas irregulares (*coast of Maine*) e hiperfunção endócrina, mais frequentemente **puberdade precoce**.

cards.front: What are the main causes of osteonecrosis (avascular necrosis), and which site is most often affected?
cards.back: Most often the **femoral head**. Causes: **glucocorticoids**, **alcohol use disorder**, **sickle cell disease**, trauma (such as femoral neck fracture), SLE, and decompression sickness. **MRI** shows it before plain x-rays change.
cards.back_pt: Mais frequentemente a **cabeça do fêmur**. Causas: **glicocorticoides**, **transtorno por uso de álcool**, **doença falciforme**, trauma (como fratura do colo do fêmur), LES e doença descompressiva. A **RM** a detecta antes de surgirem alterações na radiografia simples.

cards.front: In which part of a long bone does each classic primary bone tumor usually arise?
cards.back: **Epiphysis**: **giant cell tumor** (adults, after the growth plate closes). **Metaphysis**: **osteosarcoma** and **osteochondroma**. **Diaphysis**: **Ewing sarcoma**.
cards.back_pt: **Epífise**: **tumor de células gigantes** (adultos, após o fechamento da placa de crescimento). **Metáfise**: **osteossarcoma** e **osteocondroma**. **Diáfise**: **sarcoma de Ewing**.

cards.front: Which primary cancers cause blastic and which cause lytic bone metastases?
cards.back: Metastases are the **most common malignant tumor in bone**. **Blastic** (sclerotic): mainly **prostate** cancer. **Lytic**: **renal cell**, **thyroid**, most **lung** cancers (small cell can be blastic), and melanoma. **Breast** cancer is often **mixed**.
cards.back_pt: As metástases são o **tumor maligno mais comum no osso**. **Blásticas** (escleróticas): principalmente câncer de **próstata**. **Líticas**: carcinoma de **células renais**, **tireoide**, a maioria dos cânceres de **pulmão** (o de pequenas células pode ser blástico) e melanoma. O câncer de **mama** costuma ser **misto**.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy has 6 weeks of pain in his left thigh, low-grade fever, and weight loss. Temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). There is a warm, tender swelling over the middle of the thigh. Leukocyte count is 12,500/mm3, and the ESR is high. X-ray of the femur shows a poorly defined, moth-eaten lytic lesion in the diaphysis. Around the shaft there are several thin layers of new periosteal bone, like the layers of an onion. Biopsy shows sheets of small, round, uniform blue cells with strong membrane staining for CD99. Which genetic abnormality is most likely present in the tumor cells?
questions.explanation: This is **Ewing sarcoma**: a child with a **diaphyseal** lesion, *onion-skin* periosteal reaction, and **CD99-positive small round blue cells**. Most cases carry **t(11;22)**, which creates the **EWSR1-FLI1** fusion transcription factor. Fever and leukocytosis can mimic osteomyelitis. Loss of both RB1 alleles is linked to **osteosarcoma**, which usually arises in the **metaphysis** and makes malignant osteoid.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **sarcoma de Ewing**: criança com lesão **diafisária**, reação periosteal em *casca de cebola* (*onion skin*) e **pequenas células redondas azuis CD99-positivas**. A maioria dos casos tem a **t(11;22)**, que cria o fator de transcrição de fusão **EWSR1-FLI1**. Febre e leucocitose podem imitar osteomielite. A perda dos dois alelos do RB1 está ligada ao **osteossarcoma**, que geralmente surge na **metáfise** e produz osteoide maligno.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman has 4 months of aching pain in her right knee. The pain is worse with activity. X-ray shows an eccentric, expansile lytic lesion in the end of the distal femur that reaches the joint surface. The growth plates are closed. A thin shell of cortex surrounds the lesion, and thin internal septa give it a soap-bubble look. There is no mineralized matrix and no periosteal reaction. Biopsy shows many osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells spread evenly among plump mononuclear cells. The neoplastic mononuclear cells recruit and activate the giant cells mainly by expressing which molecule?
questions.explanation: This is a **giant cell tumor of bone**: a young adult, an **epiphyseal** lesion after growth-plate closure, a *soap-bubble* x-ray, and osteoclast-like giant cells. The **neoplastic cells are the mononuclear stromal cells**; they express **RANKL**, which recruits and activates the osteoclast-like giant cells. This is why an anti-RANKL antibody can treat this tumor. **Osteoprotegerin** is a decoy receptor that blocks RANKL, so more of it would reduce bone resorption, not drive it; PTHrP acts only indirectly, by raising RANKL on osteoblasts.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **tumor de células gigantes do osso**: adulto jovem, lesão **epifisária** após o fechamento da placa de crescimento, radiografia em *bolhas de sabão* (*soap bubble*) e células gigantes semelhantes a osteoclastos. As **células neoplásicas são as células estromais mononucleares**; elas expressam **RANKL**, que recruta e ativa as células gigantes semelhantes a osteoclastos. Por isso um anticorpo anti-RANKL pode tratar esse tumor. A **osteoprotegerina** é um receptor-isca que bloqueia o RANKL; mais dela reduziria a reabsorção óssea, e não a estimularia; o PTHrP age apenas indiretamente, ao elevar o RANKL nos osteoblastos.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man has 1 year of a deep, dull ache in his right thigh that is worse at night. His wife says his hats no longer fit, and he has trouble hearing. Serum calcium, phosphate and PTH are normal. Alkaline phosphatase is markedly high. X-ray of the right femur shows a bowed, enlarged bone with a thick cortex and coarse, disorganized trabeculae. Skull films show a thickened calvaria with patchy, fluffy dense areas. Which process best explains this disease?
choices: Failure of osteoclasts to acidify the resorption pit
Deficient mineralization of newly formed osteoid
Activating GNAS mutation in osteoblast precursors
Reduced bone mass with a normally mineralized matrix
Excess osteoclast resorption followed by disorganized new bone formation
questions.explanation: This is **Paget disease of bone**. It starts with large, overactive **osteoclasts**; osteoblasts respond and lay down thick but **disorganized bone** (a *mosaic* pattern), which is weak and deforms. Osteoblast activity explains the **isolated high alkaline phosphatase**. **Osteopetrosis** also makes dense bone, but it comes from osteoclasts that cannot resorb, usually presents in childhood, and does not enlarge or bow the bones; ALP is usually normal. **Osteomalacia** would show low calcium or phosphate and high PTH.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **doença de Paget óssea**. Começa com **osteoclastos** grandes e hiperativos; os osteoblastos respondem e depositam osso espesso, mas **desorganizado** (padrão em *mosaico*), que é fraco e se deforma. A atividade osteoblástica explica a **fosfatase alcalina elevada isoladamente**. A **osteopetrose** também produz osso denso, mas resulta de osteoclastos que não reabsorvem, geralmente aparece na infância e não aumenta nem encurva os ossos; a fosfatase alcalina costuma ser normal. A **osteomalácia** mostraria cálcio ou fósforo baixos e PTH alto.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy stepped on a nail 3 weeks ago. The nail went through the sole of his sneaker into his foot. He now has worsening pain and swelling of the forefoot. Temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F). There is tenderness over the head of the third metatarsal. X-ray of the foot shows soft-tissue swelling, a focal lytic area in the third metatarsal head, and thin new periosteal bone along the shaft. Bone biopsy culture grows an oxidase-positive gram-negative rod that does not ferment lactose. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: A nail puncture **through a sneaker** is the classic setting for **Pseudomonas aeruginosa** osteomyelitis; the organism lives in the moist foam of the shoe sole. It is an **oxidase-positive, non-lactose-fermenting gram-negative rod**. **Staphylococcus aureus** is the most common cause of osteomyelitis overall, but it is a gram-positive coccus. **Salmonella** is classic in **sickle cell disease** and is oxidase-negative; E. coli and Klebsiella ferment lactose.
questions.explanation_pt: A perfuração por prego **através do tênis** é o cenário clássico de osteomielite por **Pseudomonas aeruginosa**; o organismo vive na espuma úmida da sola do calçado. É um **bastonete gram-negativo oxidase-positivo que não fermenta lactose**. O **Staphylococcus aureus** é a causa mais comum de osteomielite em geral, mas é um coco gram-positivo. A **Salmonella** é clássica na **doença falciforme** e é oxidase-negativa; E. coli e Klebsiella fermentam lactose.

notes.title: Bone pathology: metabolic disease, infection and tumors
notes.body_md:
## Bone formation

- **Endochondral**: a cartilage model is replaced by bone (long bones, vertebrae). **Intramembranous**: bone forms directly from mesenchyme (flat skull bones, face).
- **Achondroplasia**: gain-of-function **FGFR3**; endochondral growth is impaired, limbs are short.
- PTH, RANKL and OPG: see the parathyroid block. Osteogenesis imperfecta: see the muscle and collagen block.

## Metabolic bone disease

- **Osteoporosis**: less bone, normal mineral; **all serum labs normal**.
- **Osteomalacia/rickets**: poor mineralization of osteoid, usually from vitamin D deficiency; see the parathyroid block.
- **Osteopetrosis**: osteoclasts cannot resorb (e.g. **carbonic anhydrase II** deficiency); dense, brittle bone, **pancytopenia**, cranial nerve palsies.
- **Paget disease**: overactive osteoclasts, then chaotic bone formation; **isolated high ALP**; hearing loss, larger hat size, **osteosarcoma** risk.
- **Fibrous dysplasia**: bone replaced by fibrous tissue; with café-au-lait spots and precocious puberty = **McCune-Albright** (**GNAS**).

## Osteonecrosis

- Usually the **femoral head**; glucocorticoids, alcohol, sickle cell disease, trauma. MRI detects it early.

## Osteomyelitis

- **Staphylococcus aureus**: most common overall.
- **Salmonella**: sickle cell disease.
- **Pseudomonas**: nail through a sneaker; also seen in injection drug use and diabetic foot (where *S. aureus* and mixed flora are common).
- X-ray: periosteal reaction and lysis appear after about 2 weeks; MRI is more sensitive.

## Tumors

- **Osteochondroma**: most common benign tumor; a cartilage-capped bony outgrowth whose marrow is continuous with the bone.
- **Osteoid osteoma**: small lucent nidus with sclerotic rim; night pain relieved by NSAIDs.
- **Giant cell tumor**: epiphysis of young adults; *soap-bubble* x-ray; neoplastic cells express **RANKL**.
- **Osteosarcoma**: metaphysis of adolescents (distal femur, proximal tibia); *Codman triangle* and *sunburst* pattern; risk with RB1 loss, Li-Fraumeni and Paget disease.
- **Ewing sarcoma**: diaphysis of children; *onion-skin* periosteum; CD99+, **t(11;22)**.
- **Chondrosarcoma**: older adults; pelvis and axial skeleton.
- **Metastases**: most common bone malignancy; prostate is blastic; kidney and thyroid are lytic.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Formação óssea

- **Endocondral**: um molde de cartilagem é substituído por osso (ossos longos, vértebras). **Intramembranosa**: o osso se forma diretamente do mesênquima (ossos planos do crânio, face).
- **Acondroplasia**: ganho de função do **FGFR3**; o crescimento endocondral fica prejudicado e os membros ficam curtos.
- PTH, RANKL e OPG: ver o bloco de paratireoide. Osteogênese imperfeita: ver o bloco de músculo e colágeno.

## Doença óssea metabólica

- **Osteoporose**: menos osso, mineralização normal; **todos os exames séricos normais**.
- **Osteomalácia/raquitismo**: mineralização deficiente do osteoide, geralmente por deficiência de vitamina D; ver o bloco de paratireoide.
- **Osteopetrose**: os osteoclastos não reabsorvem (p. ex., deficiência de **anidrase carbônica II**); osso denso e frágil, **pancitopenia**, paralisias de nervos cranianos.
- **Doença de Paget**: osteoclastos hiperativos, depois formação óssea caótica; **fosfatase alcalina elevada isoladamente**; perda auditiva, aumento do tamanho do chapéu, risco de **osteossarcoma**.
- **Displasia fibrosa**: osso substituído por tecido fibroso; com manchas café com leite e puberdade precoce = **McCune-Albright** (**GNAS**).

## Osteonecrose

- Geralmente na **cabeça do fêmur**; glicocorticoides, álcool, doença falciforme, trauma. A RM a detecta cedo.

## Osteomielite

- **Staphylococcus aureus**: a mais comum em geral.
- **Salmonella**: doença falciforme.
- **Pseudomonas**: prego através do tênis; também em uso de drogas injetáveis e pé diabético (onde *S. aureus* e flora mista são comuns).
- Radiografia: reação periosteal e lise surgem após cerca de 2 semanas; a RM é mais sensível.

## Tumores

- **Osteocondroma**: tumor benigno mais comum; projeção óssea com capa de cartilagem, cuja medula é contínua com a do osso.
- **Osteoma osteoide**: pequeno nicho radiotransparente com halo esclerótico; dor noturna aliviada por AINEs.
- **Tumor de células gigantes**: epífise de adultos jovens; radiografia em *bolhas de sabão* (*soap bubble*); as células neoplásicas expressam **RANKL**.
- **Osteossarcoma**: metáfise de adolescentes (fêmur distal, tíbia proximal); *triângulo de Codman* e padrão em *raios de sol* (*sunburst*); risco com perda do RB1, Li-Fraumeni e doença de Paget.
- **Sarcoma de Ewing**: diáfise de crianças; periósteo em *casca de cebola* (*onion skin*); CD99+, **t(11;22)**.
- **Condrossarcoma**: adultos mais velhos; pelve e esqueleto axial.
- **Metástases**: neoplasia maligna óssea mais comum; próstata é blástica; rim e tireoide são líticas.
